title: Green Alpha Ampalaya (Green Alpha F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Green Alpha ampalaya is an F1 hybrid ampalaya variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Green Alpha ampalaya is an F1 hybrid ampalaya variety, also sold or known as Green Alpha F1. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor brand).

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Green Alpha ampalaya is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Green Alpha F1, this is the same ampalaya. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [ampalaya variety finder](/crop-varieties/ampalaya), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest 50 to 55 days after transplanting. Yield, by the seller's count: 21.3 t/ha (company figure). No trial on record checks these figures yet, so treat them as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit ampalaya fields most often: [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly), [squash beetle](/pests/squash-beetle), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 50 to 55 days after transplanting.
**Fruit:** Straight and cylindrical, medium green with fine warts, about 41 cm long and 283 g.
Rated intermediate against cercospora leaf spot, gummy stem blight and cucurbit aphid borne yellows virus.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a long, straight fruited ampalaya in Allied Botanical's newer hybrids. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual ampalaya on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Green Alpha ampalaya

Pick by fruit: long and light green for most markets, short and dark for the bitter lovers. Hybrids yield more on a trellis, and some are bred to tolerate the downy mildew of the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: Is Green Alpha F1 the same as Green Alpha?
items.a: Yes. Green Alpha F1 is another name for Green Alpha. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Green Alpha?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
